idiom: to get to the bottom of something
meaning: to discover the real cause or truth behind a problem by investigating it thoroughly
literal_translation: докопаться до сути, выяснить настоящую причину проблемы
example: The researchers spent two years trying to get to the bottom of the anomaly in their data.
origin: Probably from the idea of digging down until one reaches solid ground; the exact origin is uncertain

wrong_meanings.meaning: to dig a hole in a garden to plant new flowers
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This takes the words literally, but the idiom describes uncovering the truth, not digging

wrong_meanings.meaning: to lower a sample into a liquid to measure its depth
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: The idiom refers to finding causes through investigation, not to physical measurement

wrong_meanings.meaning: to stop searching once the first answer has been found
wrong_meanings.why_wrong: This is the opposite of the idiom, which describes continuing until the real cause is found

explanation: 'To get to the bottom of something' means to investigate a matter until its real cause or explanation is understood. It is common in scientific writing when a study explains an unexpected result.
